reason: The cited evidence does not mention plasma nitriding, TiN/Ti2N phases, or the specific hardness/wear improvements claimed. E1 only states Ti-6Al-4V has low hardness and wear resistance, E2 describes a laser cladding method with different powders, and E3 reports hardness/wear improvements from ultrasonic burnishing, not nitriding. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Plasma nitriding at ~540°C for 4 hours forms a graded TiN/Ti2N layer on Ti-6Al-4V
This nitride layer increases surface microhardness by 30–50%
This nitride layer significantly reduces wear rates under ambient to moderately stressed conditions
The mechanism involves nitrogen diffusion, hard nitride formation, and induced compressive stresses impeding dislocation motion
